title: Read an acinar profile

regions.label: Luminal compartment
regions.observation: A central irregular pale space contains some pink material and is bounded by epithelial cells.
regions.interpretation: Use this space to orient the apical side of the surrounding epithelium before interpreting the exterior.
regions.limit: The appearance does not chemically identify every luminal constituent.

regions.label: Epithelial lining
regions.observation: Purple nuclei and surrounding cytoplasm form the lining around the central space.
regions.interpretation: The lining defines the epithelial compartment; not every cell boundary is resolved in this plane.
regions.limit: Routine H&E does not establish the expression of a specific secretion protein.

regions.label: Peripheral nuclei
regions.observation: Elongated nuclei lie near the outer edge of the profile beside pink tissue.
regions.interpretation: Their position is observable. Specific myoepithelial phenotype needs additional evidence when the identity is uncertain.
regions.limit: Do not label every peripheral nucleus as a validated myoepithelial cell.

regions.label: Surrounding stroma
regions.observation: Wavy pink bundles with scattered nuclei occupy the tissue outside the epithelial profile.
regions.interpretation: This gives connective-tissue context around the acinar structure.
regions.limit: The broad bundles are not a direct image of every basement-membrane component.

model: Locate the irregular lumen, follow the nuclear-rich epithelial lining and describe the surrounding pink stroma. Peripheral nuclei can be identified by position without claiming a confirmed cell phenotype. The provider identifies a human breast acinus, but this isolated field does not establish a whole lobule, calibrated size, hormonal state or live secretion.

title: Read lobular architecture before the overlay

regions.label: Upper H&E epithelial group
regions.observation: Numerous small epithelial profiles cluster together within a shared local stromal setting.
regions.interpretation: The grouped organization supplies lobular context that an isolated acinar close-up cannot provide.
regions.limit: A single section does not trace every ductal connection.

regions.label: Interlobular stroma
regions.observation: Broad pink tissue separates the lower-panel groups of nuclear-rich epithelial profiles.
regions.interpretation: Compare this broad matrix with the smaller spaces within each group.
regions.limit: Area fraction is not an absolute measurement of whole-organ stromal mass.

regions.label: Lower H&E lobular groups
regions.observation: Several epithelial groups appear in the lower-left field at the scale indicated by its own bar.
regions.interpretation: Use the lower 400 µm bar for this panel; the upper panel has a separate 200 µm bar.
regions.limit: These are research biopsy fields, not a documented pregnancy or lactation sequence.

regions.label: Computer-segmented compartments
regions.observation: Bright colours cover structures in the right panels while their underlying architectural outlines remain recognizable.
regions.interpretation: These colours represent algorithmic segmentation classes. Compare them with the corresponding H&E arrangement.
regions.limit: An algorithmic boundary is not a stain-specific molecular signal or guaranteed ground truth.

model: Begin with the uncoloured H&E on the left: grouped epithelial profiles contrast with broader pink interlobular tissue. Read each scale bar in its own panel. Then compare the coloured right-hand segmentation without treating it as a new stain or an error-free diagnosis. The source cohort comprises benign breast-disease biopsies and does not establish the lactational state of these displayed fields.
